correctness.rationale: A proper color class lies in a single part. If c_i classes lie in part i and q is the total, a vertex in part i wholly dominates exactly q-c_i classes. This never exceeds N-n_i and singleton coloring attains N-n_i for every i, giving feasibility k≤N-L. For fixed t=q-k the exact integer multiplicity constraints are 1≤c_i≤min(n_i,t) and sum c_i=k+t. Every integer total between r and the sum of the caps is attained by starting at all ones and adding units within the caps. Thus the least feasible t gives exactly the optimum, and all and only the indicated per-part partitions attain it. Each unordered partition into q blocks has q! distinct labelings by [q], giving the displayed Stirling sum. The one-color-per-part and two-shore cases reduce respectively to r for k≤r-1 and 2k for feasible k on K_{m,n}; singleton parts and k=N-L pose no exception. The frozen verifier and output were inspected, not executed. A separate finite census of canonical set partitions covered 40 profile–k cases on ten profiles with 2≤N≤5 and matched the minima, counts and feasibility. The unbounded claim follows from the argument, not the census.

value.rationale: The feasibility observation is routine, but the natural family is fully evaluated in the nontrivial k>r−1 regime, including exactly which part splits attain the optimum and how often. The capacity criterion and exact counts give researchers a usable benchmark for the general k-tuple coloring invariant, without enumerating proper colorings or relying on the elementary special cases for significance.
